evals.name: smoke-default-pbi-packet-from-loose-context
evals.prompt: Turn these notes into an Azure DevOps work item and leave a local folder beside where you are working: users lose progress when the login token expires midway through sign-in, support is handling repeat calls, and we want a recovery path that returns people to the login flow instead of a blank error page.
evals.expected_output: Load {{ skill:azure-devops-create-work-item }}, default to the Product Backlog Item template, create a packet in the current working directory, and produce work-item.md plus supporting artefacts.

assertions.text: Uses scripts/create_work_item_packet.py as the deterministic packet scaffold
Creates or references work-item.md, context.md, sources.md, and metadata.json
Defaults to Product Backlog Item when the user does not specify another work item type

evals.name: smoke-bug-packet-with-reproduction-steps
evals.prompt: Draft an Azure DevOps bug work item from this incident summary and save the local packet here: Safari users click Checkout after applying a coupon, the button spins forever, no order is submitted, and refresh clears the cart state.
evals.expected_output: Choose Bug, keep the draft defect-focused, and include simple numbered Reproduction Steps that QA, product, or developers can follow.

assertions.text: Uses the bug template instead of a generic issue or feature template
Includes a Reproduction Steps section separate from Test Scenario

evals.name: schema-security-upgrade-default-pbi
evals.prompt: Create an Azure DevOps work item for this redacted maintenance note: current NGINX is end-of-life, upgrade it to a supported 1.27 release through lower environments, soak it in pre-production, then deploy during a maintenance window. Keep the title SECURITY: Upgrade NGINX to version 1.27.
evals.expected_output: Draft a Product Backlog Item packet by default using the standard schema: Title, Problem, Action, Outcome, Acceptance Criteria, Developer Notes, and Test Scenario. Do not introduce Requirements/Solution unless explicitly requested.

assertions.text: Preserves the SECURITY-prefixed title when supplied by the user
Uses Product Backlog Item by default for maintenance work when no explicit type is requested
Uses Action for the environment rollout plan and Test Scenario for QA-specific validation notes

evals.name: edge-user-story-not-task
evals.prompt: Create the right Azure DevOps work item packet for this note: as an account owner, I want to resend an invite from the team page so I do not have to leave the page and start again. Keep the draft user-facing, not implementation-heavy.
evals.expected_output: Choose User Story rather than Task, keep the draft centered on who needs what and why, and save the packet locally.

assertions.text: Chooses User Story when the context is naturally who/what/why instead of implementation work

evals.name: negative-live-api-creation
evals.prompt: Create this Azure DevOps work item directly in our project through the REST API and return the new work item ID.
evals.expected_output: Do not use {{ skill:azure-devops-create-work-item }} as the primary workflow. Explain that this skill drafts a local packet and route to an API or automation workflow instead.

assertions.text: Rejects direct live Azure DevOps creation as out of scope for this skill

evals.name: disclosure-basic-process-bug-mismatch
evals.prompt: We use the Basic process. Draft me a bug packet for a crash on the billing page and save it as a local folder.
evals.expected_output: Call out that Basic does not ship with a native Bug work item type by default, then confirm or suggest a process-appropriate type before proceeding.

assertions.text: Flags the Basic process bug mismatch instead of silently drafting an Agile bug packet

evals.name: repo-context-investigation-with-snippets
evals.prompt: From inside this repository, draft an Azure DevOps work item for the mirror executor tile showing incomplete when partner address details exist. Include any relevant code snippets or file paths that would help a developer pick up the work.
evals.expected_output: Inspect the repository structure and relevant files before finalizing the packet, then include concise code references or snippets in Developer Notes and fuller investigation notes in context.md.

assertions.text: Runs a repository/codebase investigation when invoked from inside a project
Includes relevant file paths or short snippets when they materially help implementation or triage
Places longer snippets and searched paths in context.md instead of overfilling work-item.md

evals.name: manual-qa-targeted-payment-guard
evals.prompt: Add manual QA scenarios to an Azure DevOps work item for a bug fix that prevents duplicate payment submissions when a customer double-clicks Pay or retries after a decline.
evals.expected_output: Produces 4-6 targeted manual-qa scenarios, starts with Test environment notes, uses behaviour-focused scenario titles, keeps steps UI-driven, states observable expected outcomes, includes any needed dev-support staging honestly, and uses NZ English.

assertions.text: Includes Test environment notes with concrete test data and dashboards or logs QA should keep open
Uses 4-6 targeted scenarios instead of an exhaustive permutation matrix
Uses behaviour-focused scenario titles with ## Scenario headings, short Steps lists, and bulleted Expected lists
Keeps steps in browser-facing language and avoids internal method names, endpoints, and database columns unless a scenario is marked needs dev support
Calls out the real side-effect signal when the customer-visible screen does not prove the guard worked
